Week 10 In-Class Activity

Activity Information

Item Details
Week Week 10
Topic Clustering, Segmentation, and Unsupervised Learning
Marks 5 Marks
Duration 1 Hour
Attempts One Attempt Only
Access Lecturer Passcode Required

Instructions

  1. Open the Week 10 live notebook.
  2. Save a copy to your Google Drive.
  3. Complete all required tasks.
  4. Answer all interpretation questions.
  5. Submit before the activity closes.

Important Reminder

This activity tests:

  • clustering intuition
  • unsupervised learning
  • similarity and distance
  • K-Means clustering
  • PCA
  • cluster interpretation
  • analytical reasoning

This week is NOT about discovering “objective truth.”

This week is about exploratory analysis and understanding hidden structure in data.

Task 1 — Understanding Unsupervised Learning

Objective

Distinguish supervised and unsupervised learning.

Questions

Question 1

What is the main difference between supervised and unsupervised learning?

Question 2

Does clustering require labeled outcomes?

Question 3

Give one example of clustering in economics or business.

Task 2 — Load Dataset and Select Variables

Objective

Prepare data for clustering.

Instructions

Load dataset and select variables.

Expected Structure

import pandas as pd

data = pd.read_csv("country_macro_data.csv")

X = data[["Inflation",
          "GDP_Growth",
          "Debt",
          "Unemployment"]]

Questions

Question 1

Why does variable selection matter in clustering?

Question 2

Can different variables produce different clusters?

Explain briefly.

Question 3

Why should variables sometimes be scaled before clustering?

Task 3 — Train K-Means Clustering Model

Objective

Perform first clustering analysis.

Instructions

Train K-Means model using 3 clusters.

Example Structure

from sklearn.cluster import KMeans

kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=3)

kmeans.fit(X)

Extract Cluster Labels

clusters = kmeans.labels_

Questions

Question 1

Who chooses the number of clusters?

Question 2

Does K-Means “discover truth”?

Explain briefly.

Question 3

Why might different cluster numbers produce different stories?

Task 4 — Visualize Clusters

Objective

Interpret clustering visually.

Instructions

Create scatter plot using:

  • Inflation
  • GDP_Growth

Color observations using cluster labels.

Example Structure

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.scatter(data["Inflation"],
            data["GDP_Growth"],
            c=clusters)

plt.xlabel("Inflation")
plt.ylabel("GDP Growth")

plt.show()

Questions

Question 1

Do clusters appear clearly separated?

Question 2

Are there overlapping observations?

Question 3

Which observations appear unusual?

Task 5 — Cluster Interpretation

Objective

Interpret cluster meaning economically.

Instructions

Describe each cluster economically.

Example:

Cluster Interpretation
Cluster 1 Stable economies
Cluster 2 High inflation economies
Cluster 3 Crisis economies

Questions

Question 1

What characteristics define each cluster?

Question 2

Why does economic interpretation matter?

Question 3

Can algorithms automatically explain economic meaning?

Task 6 — Apply PCA

Objective

Reduce dimensions for visualization.

Instructions

Apply PCA using 2 components.

Example Structure

from sklearn.decomposition import PCA

pca = PCA(n_components=2)

principal_components = pca.fit_transform(X)

Visualize PCA Output

plt.scatter(principal_components[:,0],
            principal_components[:,1],
            c=clusters)

plt.show()

Questions

Question 1

What is the purpose of PCA?

Question 2

Does dimensionality reduction simplify interpretation?

Question 3

What information might be lost during dimensionality reduction?

Task 7 — Experiment with Cluster Numbers

Objective

Understand sensitivity of clustering.

Instructions

Compare:

  • 2 clusters
  • 3 clusters
  • 5 clusters

Questions

Question 1

Do cluster structures change?

Question 2

Which number of clusters appears most interpretable?

Question 3

Why is there no universally “correct” number of clusters?

Reflection Question

Write a short paragraph answering:

Why should economists critically evaluate clustering results instead of treating algorithmic groups as objective truths?

Your answer should include:

  • assumptions
  • variable selection
  • interpretation
  • scaling
  • policy implications

Common Errors

Problem 1 — Ignoring Scaling

Variables with large values may dominate clustering unfairly.

Problem 2 — Treating Clusters as Objective Truth

Clusters are constructed statistical groupings.

They are NOT natural truths.

Problem 3 — Weak Interpretation

Algorithms alone do NOT explain economic meaning.

Interpretation requires context and judgment.

Problem 4 — Too Many Clusters

Too many clusters reduce interpretability.

Problem 5 — Blind Trust in Visualization

Visual separation may exaggerate actual structure.
